snapshot_note: Commercial marketing tools compared on SwapToMartech.

hubspot.name: HubSpot
hubspot.billing_unit: base edition fee + per Core Seat + per 5,000-contact block + metered AI credits
hubspot.why_look_for_alternatives: Pricing scales aggressively with contacts and seats. Onboarding fee is mandatory. Feature bundling forces users to pay for modules they don't use.

mailchimp.name: Mailchimp
mailchimp.why_look_for_alternatives: Price jumps sharply once contact list grows past 500. Automation limited on lower tiers. Free plan capped at 500 contacts (down from 2000).

ahrefs.name: Ahrefs
ahrefs.billing_unit: flat plan fee + metered report credits + fixed-price capped seats
ahrefs.why_look_for_alternatives: Ahrefs raised prices multiple times in 2023-2025. Starter plan lost bulk features. Costs $1500+/year even at entry.

semrush.name: Semrush
semrush.why_look_for_alternatives: Similar to Ahrefs but more feature-bloated. Entry tier limits are aggressive.

calendly.name: Calendly
calendly.why_look_for_alternatives: Per-seat pricing multiplies across a team, and the free tier's 1-event-type limit pushes most real users to paid immediately.

zapier.name: Zapier
zapier.why_look_for_alternatives: Billing counts action steps, not workflow runs, so cost scales with workflow complexity rather than business volume. Adding a filter or formatter step to an existing Zap raises the bill without doing more work.

hootsuite.name: Hootsuite
hootsuite.why_look_for_alternatives: Pricing multiplies linearly per seat while the underlying job — queueing posts to public social APIs — has no proprietary data moat. Three seats cost roughly six times what the equivalent server does.

notion.name: Notion
notion.why_look_for_alternatives: Per-seat pricing on a document store, where the underlying capability (structured docs in a database) has open-source equivalents.

slack.name: Slack
slack.why_look_for_alternatives: Per-seat pricing where the binding constraint is message retention, which is a storage problem rather than a proprietary capability.

loom.name: Loom
loom.why_look_for_alternatives: Screen recording and hosting is commodity capability; the per-seat charge scales with team size while storage cost does not.

intercom.name: Intercom
intercom.why_look_for_alternatives: Seat pricing plus an uncapped AI meter; the inbox itself is replaceable but the AI resolution cost follows you.

airtable.name: Airtable
airtable.why_look_for_alternatives: Per-seat pricing on a shared database, where the underlying capability is a Postgres table with a grid UI on top - and where the API throughput you may actually be hitting the wall on cannot be bought at any tier.

chatwoot.name: Chatwoot
chatwoot.why_look_for_alternatives: Seat pricing scales linearly; 10+ agent teams pay $4,680–$11,880/yr on Business/Enterprise tiers

launchdarkly.name: LaunchDarkly
launchdarkly.billing_unit: client-side MAU (per 1K) + AI runs + service connections
launchdarkly.why_look_for_alternatives: Client-side MAU pricing scales quickly. 10K MAU = $1,200/year. Enterprise features (SCIM, approvals, 100+ day retention) require custom pricing.

growthbook.name: GrowthBook
growthbook.billing_unit: per seat + CDN requests overage + CDN bandwidth overage
growthbook.why_look_for_alternatives: Seat-based pricing scales with team size. 10 seats = $4,800/year. Their own FAQ says 'pay for the people who run experiments, not the end users' but that hurts at scale.

statsig.name: Statsig
statsig.why_look_for_alternatives: Baseline fee + event-based pricing. Even with no events, you pay $1,800/year. High-traffic apps can rack up overage charges.

klaviyo.name: Klaviyo
klaviyo.billing_unit: per profile tier + send volume cap (dual gates)
klaviyo.why_look_for_alternatives: Most expensive ESP per contact. Charges for inactive profiles. Send volume caps create surprise upgrade pressure. Core segmentation + automation available in cheaper alternatives.

activecampaign.name: ActiveCampaign
activecampaign.why_look_for_alternatives: Expensive at scale (25k contacts = $4,668 to $10,548/year depending on tier). CRM bundling forces payment for unused features. Automation builder has steep learning curve.

emailoctopus.name: EmailOctopus
emailoctopus.why_look_for_alternatives: No revenue attribution. No SMS. Automation builder simpler than Klaviyo. Best for teams that do not need advanced e-commerce features.

mailerlite.name: MailerLite
mailerlite.why_look_for_alternatives: Limited automation depth. No revenue tracking. Good for content marketers, weak for e-commerce attribution.

brevo.name: Brevo
brevo.why_look_for_alternatives: Send-volume pricing can surprise high-frequency senders. UI less polished than Klaviyo. No revenue attribution.

postmark.name: Postmark
postmark.description: Transactional email service focused on delivery speed and reliability. Offers detailed analytics, bounce/spam complaint tracking, and dedicated support.
postmark.why_look_for_alternatives: Postmark costs $1,200/year for 100K emails vs SES Essentials at $192/year. But self-hosting costs $7,200/year in server + DevOps time. This is the rare case where the cheapest option is still a SaaS.

amazon-ses.name: Amazon SES
amazon-ses.description: AWS transactional email service. Pay-as-you-go pricing with no base fee. New accounts default to Essentials plan ($0.16/1K). Legacy à la carte ($0.10/1K) only available to accounts with metered activity before June 1, 2025.
amazon-ses.why_look_for_alternatives: SES Essentials is already the cheapest transactional email option at $192/year for 100K emails. The only reason to look elsewhere is if you need dedicated support, which SES does not provide.

mailgun.name: Mailgun
mailgun.description: Transactional email API service. Note: pricing varies by region (USD/EUR/GBP) with independent rates, not currency conversion.
mailgun.why_look_for_alternatives: Mailgun Foundation costs $420/year for 50K emails. SES Essentials costs $96/year for the same volume. Unless you specifically need Mailgun's validation API or EU data residency, SES is cheaper.

sendgrid.name: SendGrid
sendgrid.description: Transactional email service, now part of Twilio. Pricing has moved to twilio.com domain. Old sendgrid.com/pricing links are dead.
sendgrid.why_look_for_alternatives: SendGrid pricing has moved to Twilio's domain. For basic transactional email, SES Essentials is cheaper and simpler.

typeform.name: Typeform
typeform.why_look_for_alternatives: Per-response pricing explodes with volume: the response base is the meter, and exceeding it forces a tier jump, not an overage rate. Self-hosted Formbricks removes response and seat caps entirely; the arbitrage is real because surveys are commodity CRUD on Postgres with no data moat.
